# A limb less than a two-limb number

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `lt_1_2` · proved for finite operands · proved for infinite and NaN operands · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

Whether $a < y$, for the exact values:

$$m = [\, a < y \,].$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $y = y_0 + y_1$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `a < y` | `T`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | `bool` |  |
| `y > a` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | `bool` |  |
| `x < y` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | `bool` | the limb of the `Expansion<T, 1>` operand is the limb $a$ |
| `y > x` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | `bool` | the limb of the `Expansion<T, 1>` operand is the limb $a$ |
| `X.certainly_positive()` | `Ball<T, 2>` | `bool` | whether every member of the ball is positive: $r < c$, exactly; false for the empty set and the whole line; `constexpr`; does not round |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $y$ is normalized: $y_0 = \mathrm{RN}(y_0 + y_1)$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $m$ is true exactly when $a < y$, for the exact values.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `lt_1_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/Compare.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/Compare.v), against `lt_1_2_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions lt_1_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition lt_1_2_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall a y0 y1 : R,
  fmt emin prec a ->
  normalized_2 emin prec y0 y1 ->
  let m := lt_1_2 a y0 y1 in
  m = Rlt_bool a (y0 + y1).
```

## Infinite and NaN operands

The statement above is about finite operands. The claims also say what the kernel returns when its operands may be infinite or NaN. That statement requires:

- $a$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.
- $y$ is canonical: finite and normalized, or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$, or $(\mathrm{NaN}, \mathrm{NaN})$.

and then:

- $m$ is true exactly when $a < y$ holds between the two values as extended real numbers ($-\infty$ below every real number, $+\infty$ above), and false when an operand is a NaN.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

**Status of this statement:** proved. Rocq checks the theorem `lt_1_2_ieee_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeExt.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeExt.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions lt_1_2_ieee_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proofs of `lt_1_2_correct` and `lt_1_2_ieee_correct` depend on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** limbs compared in order (Milestone 1 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/lt_1_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/lt_1_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# a < y: lt_2_2 with (a, 0) in place of x.

h = lt(a, y0)
e = eq(a, y0)
l = lt(0, y1)
t = and(e, l)
m = or(h, t)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone1/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone1/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone1.md#lt_1_2)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 60 runners on 3 machines | 110 400 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 60 runners on 3 machines | 110 400 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 6 domains of 6 formats | 11 490 416 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand, supplementary run: 1 domain of 1 format | 896 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements of the statement on infinite and NaN operands.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only limbs given by the program can make: `from_limbs` in a build without checks, `from_limbs_unchecked`, or `limb[]` written directly.
